tour.name: Mexico City Private Tour: the Zócalo, Templo Mayor, Diego Rivera Murals & the Anthropology Museum
tour.subtitle: Mexico City's Aztec and colonial heart in one private day with a licensed guide and vehicle: the Zócalo and the Metropolitan Cathedral, the ruins of the Templo Mayor, Diego Rivera's murals in the National Palace, the Palacio de Bellas Artes, tacos al pastor, and the treasures of the National Museum of Anthropology.

tour.overview:
Mexico City stands on the site of Tenochtitlan, the island capital of the Aztecs, founded around 1325 in a lake. The Spanish conquerors built their capital on its ruins, and the cathedral and palaces of the Zócalo rise beside the excavated remains of the Templo Mayor, the Aztecs' great twin temple. Together with Xochimilco, the historic centre is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In Chapultepec, the National Museum of Anthropology holds the world's greatest collection of ancient Mexican art.

This private day shows the city with a licensed guide and a vehicle, from Aztec ruins to modern murals.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Mexico City
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, vehicle and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Zócalo and the cathedral.
• The Templo Mayor.
• The National Palace murals.
• Bellas Artes.
• The National Museum of Anthropology.

WHY THIS WORKS
The city is vast and its traffic heavy; your driver and guide make the most of the day and the museum’s highlights.

WHO IT SUITS
History and art lovers, families and first-time visitors.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For Frida Kahlo and Xochimilco, choose our Coyoacán and Xochimilco tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Mexico City is at 2,240 metres; take it easy on your first day. The Anthropology Museum is closed on Mondays.

days.name: The Zócalo, the Templo Mayor, the National Palace, Bellas Artes and the Anthropology Museum
days.description:
What to expect: Aztec and colonial Mexico City and its great museum, with a licensed guide, private vehicle, entrances and a tasting.

Your guide and driver collect you at about 9:00 and drive to the Zócalo, the vast main square with its giant flag. You visit the Metropolitan Cathedral, built over nearly 250 years, and see how its floor tilts as the city sinks into the old lake bed. Next door, the ruins of the Templo Mayor reveal layer upon layer of the Aztec temple to the gods Huitzilopochtli and Tlaloc, and its museum shows the great stone disc of the moon goddess Coyolxauhqui. In the National Palace, Diego Rivera's murals on the main staircase tell the history of Mexico from the Aztecs to the 20th century.

You walk along Madero Street to the Palacio de Bellas Artes, with its Art Nouveau exterior and Art Deco interior, and taste tacos al pastor, pork cooked on a vertical spit with pineapple, at a local taquería.

In the afternoon, your driver takes you to Chapultepec for the National Museum of Anthropology. Your guide leads you to its masterpieces: the Aztec Sun Stone, the colossal Olmec heads, the replica of the tomb of the Maya king Pakal and the giant statue of Tlaloc at the entrance, before returning to your hotel.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
09:00 – Pick-up at your hotel.
09:30 – Zócalo and cathedral.
10:30 – Templo Mayor.
11:45 – National Palace murals.
12:30 – Bellas Artes and taco tasting.
14:30 – National Museum of Anthropology.
17:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The National Palace sometimes closes for official events; the Rivera murals at the Secretariat of Education are an alternative.
• Drink bottled water only.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, licensed guide, entrances, taco tasting, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: tasting.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Are entrances included?
faq.answer: Yes: the Templo Mayor and the National Museum of Anthropology.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: A taco tasting is; a fuller lunch is extra.

faq.question: Is Mexico City safe?
faq.answer: With a local guide and a private vehicle, yes. Keep valuables out of sight.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the Aztec stones and the tacos.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. The museum and the Zócalo are accessible.

faq.question: Does the tour run on Mondays?
faq.answer: Yes, but the museums are closed; we adapt the itinerary.

faq.question: Will the altitude affect us?
faq.answer: Some people feel tired at 2,240 metres; drink water and take it easy.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes, layers and sun protection.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: October to May, the dry season.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is customary in Mexico: 10 to 15 percent for guides and drivers is usual if you were happy with the service, but it is always your choice.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
